transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, thank you for seeing me. I guess… what brings me in is that I’ve just been really tired. I mean, I’m still functioning, going to work and all that, but it feels harder than it should. Sleep doesn’t really seem to fix it, and even getting through a normal workday and then dinner at home feels kind of heavy. I’m not sure if that’s the right way to describe it.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, because I’m still doing what I need to do, but most days lately I wake up with this kind of heavy, gray feeling. Like I’m already disappointed in the day before it’s even really started, if that makes sense.
Have you been enjoying things less than you usually do?

Yeah… a little, I think. I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, but I usually really love painting, and I like wandering through museum exhibits when I have time. Lately my supplies just kind of sit there untouched, and even the idea of going to a museum feels like… more effort than I can get myself to care about. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been feeling this way most days for at least two weeks?

Yes… I think so. It’s probably been about a month altogether. It kind of shifted from a period where I was unusually energized and really driven, and then this lower feeling settled in and has been there most days since. I hope that’s the sort of timeframe you mean.
During that unusually energized period, did you need much less sleep than usual?

Yes… I guess I did. I didn’t really think of it as a problem at the time, because I felt fine—better than fine, honestly. I was sleeping maybe four hours, and then I’d get up feeling ready to send emails, sketch out event ideas, or even reorganize the kitchen. It sounds like a lot when I say it out loud, but it felt productive then.
During that energized period, did you feel unusually confident or powerful, like you could do things other people couldn’t?

Maybe a bit, yes. I don’t know if I’d call it powerful exactly, but I was… very sure I had the answers. Like, I honestly thought I could fix the whole department morale issue at work and get our family routines running perfectly, if everyone would just listen and get on board with my plan. At the time it felt reasonable, but saying it now, I can see it might have been a little much.
During that unusually energized period, were you hospitalized because of it?

No, no hospitalization or anything like that. It didn’t get to that level, at least not as far as I’d understand it. I was still going to work and managing things… maybe not perfectly, but no one took me to a hospital or suggested that. Is that what you mean?
During that energized period, did it cause serious problems in your life or work?

Not serious, I don’t think… I mean, I was still showing up for work and taking care of things at home. So I wouldn’t want to make it sound dramatic.

But, yes, maybe there were some effects. I was slower making decisions at work, and at home I got a little less reliable with family plans than I’d like to admit. And I kind of pulled back from my art activities, which usually help me stay connected with people. So… not a disaster, but not nothing either, I guess. Does that make sense?
About how many days did that unusually energized period last?

I’m trying to count it accurately… it wasn’t just a couple of days. The energized, driven part and then the low part all together has been about a month, I’d say. Maybe the more “up” part felt shorter within that, but this whole swing has been going on around four weeks. Is that the kind of timeframe you mean?
Did that unusually energized period last at least 4 days?

Yes… I think so. I mean, the whole recent swing — from feeling unusually energized and driven and then into feeling low — has been going on about a month. So the energized part was definitely not just a day or two. I hope that answers it the right way.
Did that unusually energized period last at least 7 days?

I think… yes, probably. I’m a little hesitant because I don’t want to overstate it, but this whole swing from being unusually energized and driven into feeling low has been going on for about a month. So I don’t think it was less than a week. Does that make sense?
During that unusually energized period, did you have any hallucinations or delusional beliefs?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I felt more energized and maybe a bit unlike myself, but I wasn’t seeing things or hearing things, and I don’t think I believed anything that wasn’t real. At least not that I’m aware of… is that what you mean?
During that unusually energized period, did your behavior cause marked problems in your work, home life, or relationships?

Not marked, I don’t think… I mean, I was still going to work and keeping up with things at home, mostly. But I guess I wasn’t functioning quite like myself. I was slower making decisions, and with my family I got less reliable about plans, which I feel bad about. And I kind of pulled back from the art stuff I usually do to stay connected.

So… not a total breakdown or anything, but yes, it did affect things some. Does that sound like what you’re asking?
During that unusually energized period, did your symptoms make you unable to do your job or usual responsibilities?

No, I wouldn’t say unable. I was still showing up for work and handling things at home, at least basically. But I wasn’t quite at my normal level… decisions took me longer, and I was less dependable with family plans than I’d like to admit. I also kind of stopped doing the art activities that usually keep me connected. So it affected me, but I don’t think it made me unable to function, if that’s the distinction you mean.
During that energized period, did other people clearly notice you were acting unusually different from your normal self?

Yes… I think a few people did notice. I don’t think I was completely out of control or anything, but my husband mentioned it, and a couple of coworkers too, that I was talking really fast and kind of jumping in so much they couldn’t really get a word in. I felt embarrassed when they said that, honestly. Is that the kind of “noticeably different” you mean?
